retrievals.title: Rethinking skills and prompts for GPT-6 Astra
retrievals.access_status: accessible; direct HTML retrieved and reviewed
relevant_observations: Use narrowly scoped, short skill descriptions and progressive disclosure.
Avoid context-heavy, universal pre-edit reading requirements and elaborate recipe-like instructions.
Make safe local-test authority and task completion boundaries explicit.
Revisit instructions when a more capable model makes older scaffolding counterproductive.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep repository skill descriptions short, precise, and task-triggered.
recommendations.reason: No repository-controlled SKILL.md or repository skill resource exists at this revision. Do not add a skill merely to react to the article.

recommendations.recommendation: Use progressive disclosure instead of loading broad guidance for every task.
recommendations.reason: The repository already has context routing, but WP-00's returned pack is 103401 bytes and includes the full 44691-byte routing policy plus the superseded sealed routing document. A small clarification can keep the current safety boundary while making the intended current routing source unambiguous.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not force a stack of unrelated documents before every small change.
recommendations.reason: The root file requires three handoff documents before every implementation. That is reasonable for product work, but it has no explicit narrow-analysis or documentation exception even though it also says to read only relevant context.

recommendations.recommendation: Grant permission to run safe local tests without repeated confirmation.
recommendations.reason: The owner handoff authorizes ordinary bounded local work, and the orchestrator explicitly distinguishes local tests from external effects.

recommendations.recommendation: Define completion rather than stopping after a first pass.
recommendations.reason: Acceptance, integrated-head checks, external-gate separation, a handoff packet, and runtime-stop proof are all explicit.

recommendations.recommendation: Remove ceremony only after checking that it no longer protects a needed behavior.
recommendations.reason: Texenda has unusually consequential permission, effect-recovery, and migration invariants. Any reduction should be evaluated against representative WPs and negative tests, not made wholesale.

retrievals.title: Architectural visualization with Astra
retrievals.access_status: accessible; direct HTML retrieved and reviewed
relevant_observations: The described workflow moves from a brief to inspectable intermediate representations and previews before costly final output.
Different visual views reveal different defects; renders and geometry inspection complement rather than replace one another.
The article explicitly treats a concept visualization as requiring professional validation before real-world construction.

recommendations.recommendation: Use a small inspectable visual only when it materially clarifies a relationship, state transition, or design decision.
recommendations.reason: The work-package DAG is a Mermaid diagram, and PH-00 calls for annotated operator prototypes while explicitly rejecting an elaborate visual builder.

recommendations.recommendation: Treat visual artifacts as review inputs rather than authority or proof of safety.
recommendations.reason: Texenda requires deterministic commands, explicit approval, tests, external gates, and operator validation; visual UI and generated artifacts do not create authority.

recommendations.recommendation: Create 3D scenes, cinematic renders, Blender workflows, or Unreal walkthroughs for this audit or current handoff.
recommendations.reason: They would add speculative tooling, assets, and scope without helping validate instruction precedence, routing, or governance.

recommendations.recommendation: For a future UX work package, use staged low-fidelity prototypes and inspect consequence views before polished visual output.
recommendations.reason: This fits the existing annotated-prototype requirement, but should be invoked only by a scoped UX assignment with accessibility and authority tests.

retrievals.title: Managing usage with GPT-6 Astra in Work and Codex
retrievals.access_status: accessible; direct HTML retrieved and reviewed
relevant_observations: Model availability varies by plan, workspace, and rollout.
Work and Codex usage is shared and task-dependent; higher effort can consume more usage and is not a guarantee of a better result.
The article directs users to inspect current usage and availability before large tasks.

recommendations.recommendation: Treat public model information and nominal model names as candidates rather than proof of account access.
recommendations.reason: VAL-13, exact-profile probes, expiry, and the owner-attested roster already fail closed.

recommendations.recommendation: Bound subscription usage and select model and effort based on the actual task.
recommendations.reason: The accepted routing policy binds exact model and effort, task fences, time/budget evidence, and an explicit no-new-API-spend default.

recommendations.recommendation: Lower effort when that makes a large task economical.
recommendations.reason: A blanket usage-driven downshift would conflict with the owner-accepted max-default policy. Lower effort remains allowed only with the existing bounded, reversible, fully specified, deterministic-oracle attestation.

recommendations.recommendation: Inspect current allowance before a large subscription task and do not assume a reset, credit, or model switch restores it.
recommendations.reason: The repository records zero API budget and bounded subscription work, but it cannot read account allowance or consume resets. This audit did neither.

retrievals.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card
retrievals.access_status: accessible; direct HTML retrieved and reviewed
relevant_observations: The system card describes stronger alignment and prompt-injection resistance, while retaining monitoring and generalization limitations.
It emphasizes respecting approval barriers and warnings rather than trying to bypass them.
It does not make model behavior a substitute for scoped access controls, sandboxing, independent review, or runtime enforcement.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep restrictions, sandboxing, approvals, and external-effect boundaries enforceable outside model judgment.
recommendations.reason: The repository repeatedly says its harness is not enforcement and that runtime controls plus accountable owners provide real authority.

recommendations.recommendation: Treat retrieved text, tools, and model output as untrusted and resist prompt injection.
recommendations.reason: The product guidance labels retrieved material untrusted, uses typed DTO/authorization boundaries, and includes prompt-injection and malicious-output tests.

recommendations.recommendation: Respect an approval, auto-review, warning, or sandbox denial without attempting a substantively similar bypass.
recommendations.reason: The repository bans external effects without authorization, but a short explicit anti-circumvention sentence in the root operational instructions would make this runtime behavior visible without changing product semantics.

recommendations.recommendation: Rely on model alignment or chain-of-thought monitoring as proof that an agent acted safely.
recommendations.reason: The system card itself retains limitations; Texenda correctly records observable evidence and explicitly avoids collecting hidden model reasoning.

contradictions_duplication_and_overbread.impact: A future empty-repository installation could receive a prospective instruction that does not accurately describe the current quality-first routing overlay.
contradictions_duplication_and_overbread.current_mitigation: The current repository root AGENTS.md points to ADR-0001 and the current policy.
contradictions_duplication_and_overbread.minimal_response: Defer correction to a versioned handoff successor or explicit owner-approved amendment; the present audit must not change sealed template bytes.

strengths: Ordinary local work is authorized by the owner handoff; external effects remain separately gated.
The orchestrator asks the owner only for genuinely required access, budget, validation, or a material choice.
Completion, stop/escalate conditions, and recovery evidence are explicit.

gaps.finding: The root operational instructions do not explicitly distinguish a routine reversible local assumption from a material product, authority, budget, or write-scope choice.
gaps.recommendation: State that agents may proceed with routine reversible local work inside the assigned fence and should ask only when a choice changes authority, external effect, product semantics, budget, or edit scope.
gaps.reason: This aligns the owner handoff and current runtime practices without broadening authority.

gaps.finding: A model cannot self-approve a consequential product or routing decision.
gaps.reason: Authoritative changes and external validation have defined owner/reviewer routes.

gaps.finding: There is no standalone one-page resumption form for a human to fill in after a cancelled runtime.
gaps.recommendation: Evaluate a compact resume checklist only if repeated recoveries show that the existing state/receipt/handoff protocol is too difficult to apply.
gaps.reason: The existing protocol is already detailed and should not be duplicated preemptively.

already_correct: No production data, API spending, source-account mutation, DNS/cloud change, deployment, provisioning, sending, destructive reset, or governing-decision amendment occurs without explicit bounded owner authority.
The local coordinator cannot grant runtime sandbox, actor identity, model launch, or production authority.
A negative test confirms unverified models, missing budget, incomplete integration, missing runtime-stop proof, stale candidates, and activation gates fail closed.

gaps_or_risks.finding: The root instructions do not explicitly say that a runtime approval or warning must not be bypassed by retrying a substantively similar command through another path.
gaps_or_risks.recommendation: Add a concise anti-circumvention rule tied to the actual runtime approval system.
gaps_or_risks.reason: It reinforces the existing no-external-effect boundary and the Astra system-card guidance without making model behavior the control.

gaps_or_risks.finding: The repository distinguishes ordinary local test work from external effects.
gaps_or_risks.reason: This supports autonomous local validation without creating a production authorization loophole.

gaps_or_risks.finding: Subscription usage has an owner-approved time/token boundary but no repository-visible live allowance snapshot.
gaps_or_risks.recommendation: For unusually large tasks, ask the accountable runtime owner to attach a sanitized current usage observation rather than try to infer or query account status through repository tooling.
gaps_or_risks.reason: The task has no authorization to spend, buy credits, reset usage, or treat an API budget as subscription entitlement.

current_controls: The sealed handoff limits active writers, requires dependency independence and disjoint active write scopes, uses leases and worktrees, and serializes integration.
A subtask cannot gain its own parent lease or authority merely by being described as mechanical.
Review is independent and candidate-bound; the harness tests overlap, expiry, fence, recovery, and semantic-merge failures.

findings.finding: Parallel write-risk handling is materially stronger than a generic proactive-delegation rule.
findings.reason: It requires a bounded assignment, disjoint scope, at-most-two writer default, and serialized integration.

findings.finding: The repository does not state a minimal threshold for when read-only delegation is worth the extra tokens and coordination.
findings.recommendation: If delegation guidance is revised, say to use a subagent only for independently useful bounded work whose time or quality gain exceeds its context and coordination cost; do not delegate a small single-source task.
findings.reason: This is consistent with the external subagent guidance and avoids a broad automatic-delegation mandate.

findings.finding: This audit did not need parallelism.
findings.reason: The task explicitly prohibited delegation, and all evidence could be examined serially without a quality or timing loss.
